messages:
sana: Heads-up — hardware partner (EdgeBox Inc.) flagged a mismatch between entitlements we send in the marketplace export and the SKUs they consume. They say some customers show as 'basic-dev' on our side but billed as 'dev-basic-v2' on their side leading to wrong plan pricing. cc @leo for mapping rules.

leo: Do we have a sample of the entitlement payload they received? my first guess: we changed the canonical sku tag in 2025-11 but kept backward aliases during onboarding; partner may be matching against exact string.

isabel: partner pasted this from their billing logs: `customer=C-909 sku=dev-basic-v2 period=2026-02-01 usage=12345` while our export row was `customer_id=C-909 entitlement=basic-dev units=12345`. they do an exact join on sku->price lookup.

sana: that's a mapping problem. we publish `entitlement_aliases.csv` but it's not included in the marketplace export artifact.

james: partner ops says they can't reliably map aliases because their pricing engine uses a strict namespace and they don't want to add fuzzy matching. they need a canonical SKU field we control.

leo: proposal: two short-term fixes and one long-term change. Short-term A) include `canonical_sku` in daily export (string) where we resolve alias->canonical; Short-term B) ship a small one-off mapping file pushed to partners via S3 with checksum. Long-term: add SKU aliasing to our contract/schema and a versioned SKU registry with GUIDs.

isabel: +1 short-term A. we already run alias resolution in the billing pipeline; adding `canonical_sku` shouldn't be invasive. I'll open a PR.

marketplace-bot: export `marketplace-usage-daily` completed 2026-03-15T02:00Z rows=45,678 errors=0 artifacts=[usage.csv] :white_check_mark:

leo: quick QA checklist: 1) ensure `canonical_sku` entries are stable for a rolling 30d window, 2) add `sku_version` and `sku_guid` fields so partners can detect changes, 3) surface mapping failures to partner on ingest with a `sku_unmapped` flag.

james: partner asked for an interoperability test. suggested test: we send a sample 2-week export with the new `canonical_sku` fields and a mapping S3 link, partner will replay to their billing engine and compare totals. they want a signed checksum file so their ingest fails loudly if mismatch.

sana: action items: isabel to PR exporter change and add `sku_guid` + `canonical_sku`; leo to draft S3 mapping file format and signed-checksum process; james to coordinate partner replay window and acceptance criteria. finance wants an illustrative customer letter if any invoices will be adjusted.

isabel: PR opened: `github.com/redwood/integrations/pull/912` includes schema change and test vectors. snippet of new row:```csv
customer_id,period,entitlement,canonical_sku,sku_guid,units
C-909,2026-02,basic-dev,dev-basic-v2,sku-0a1b2c,12345
```

leo: test plan: run partner-replay for C-909 and 10 more customers with known alias histories. compare `billed_amount` before/after. Expect zero change if partner applies canonical mapping correctly. If partner had been applying incorrect prices, we'll see delta.

marketplace-bot: scheduled job `sku-registry-sync` will run at 2026-03-16T06:00Z to publish `sku_registry_v2026-03-16.json` to `s3://partner-artifacts/edgebox/`

james: partner ops confirmed they'll ingest the sample file tomorrow and will report mismatches within 48h. they asked for a rollback plan: if the new canonical field causes unexpected pricing spikes on their side, they want us to pause and revert.

sana: agreed — we'll gate rollout behind the partner test and have finance accept any credit workflow. also add a monitoring alert if daily spend for partner customers changes by >5% post-rollout.

leo: i'll add a quick reconciliation job to compare `export.units * price_lookup(canonical_sku)` vs partner `billed_amount` for a sample window and emit a CSV of mismatches. will post results here.

isabel: thanks all. PR includes test vectors and docs. linking to PR and S3 spec in follow-up message.

sana: nice work. keeping this thread open until partner confirms replay OK and finance approves any adjustments.
